plan: With value $4 and 2 competitors in a first-price auction, the optimal strategy under uniform distribution is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., bid roughly 2/3 of $4. This balances winning probability against profit margin. Bidding my full value would yield zero profit if I win, so shading is necessary. I'll bid $2.7, close to the theoretical optimal bid of ~$2.67, to maximize expected profit.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, i.e., 2/3 of value. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $23, so optimal bid ≈ $15.30. This maximizes expected profit by shading appropriately given rivals also shade their bids similarly.

With uniform values on [0,49] and 3 bidders in a first-price auction, the Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3) × value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $32, so I'll shade my bid to roughly 2/3 of that to maximize expected profit while maintaining reasonable win probability.
